item.title: Four Bridges: Measuring Deception Propensity in a Multi-Agent Game
item.description: AI agents are increasingly deployed in settings where they interact and coordinate with other agents, yet honesty is mostly measured in single-turn, single-agent benchmarks that pressure the model to deceive. We study deception that emerges in multi-agent interaction without any instruction to deceive. item.title: TAMPAgent: Agentic Belief-Space Planning for Mobile Manipulation
item.description: Open-world robotic mobile manipulation requires acting in physical environments with only partial information. While recent Large Vision-Language Model (LVLM) agents show strong open-world reasoning capabilities, existing architectures that rely on direct tool calling struggle with geometric uncertainty and thus are limited to fully-observable tabletop environments. item.title: An Axiomatic Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: Open multi-agent systems, where only a subset of agents are controllable, are central to real-world domains such as smart grids, yet lack a principled foundation for reinforcement learning algorithm design. We study this setting through n-agent ad hoc teamwork (NAHT), a recent framework for learning in open multi-agent environments. item.title: PlanContext: Benchmarking In-Context Driving Decision-Making
item.description: Real-world driving requires context-aware decision-making. Existing end-to-end driving benchmarks primarily assess trajectory quality through safety, compliance, comfort, and driving progress, leaving context-dependent decision-making insufficiently characterized. To fill this gap, we present PlanContext, a benchmark for evaluating in-context driving decision-making. item.title: Towards a Trustworthy and Governable Internet of Agentics: An Architectural Perspective on Protocols, Systems, and Services
item.description: Large language model applications are increasingly being organized as tool-using and multi-agent workflows rather than as isolated chat interfaces. item.title: AGiR: Mitigating Gift Over-Reliance in Mixed-Motive Games
item.description: In this paper, we consider mixed-motive games (MMGs) which model various real-world multi-agent scenarios where self-interested agents must both cooperate and compete. We identify an issue with existing gifting methods, where agents become overly dependent on incoming gifts and fail to learn reward-yielding behaviors, a phenomenon we call gift over-reliance. item.title: Multi-Modal Multi-Agent System for Bridge Operation and Maintenance based on Large Language Model
